Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

provide verb

supply, give

also supply, provide with, furnish, make available

classical

Liv. 5.55.3: tēgula pūblicē praebita est
Cato Agr. 14: quae opus sunt dominus praebēbit

praebeō, praebēre, praebuī, praebitum

verb, second conjugation

provide, supply, offer

With the dative of the person provided for: alicui aliquid praebēre. Things provide too: quae praebet lātās arbor spatiantibus umbrās, the tree that gives wide shade to those who walk under it (Ov. Rem. 85).

Other words

  • suppeditō, suppeditāre, suppeditāvī, suppeditātum — supply in plenty; be on hand

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.12: ea, quae suppeditent ad cultum et ad victum

    Transitive, to supply; intransitive, of things that are there in plenty.

  • īnstruō, īnstruere, īnstrūxī, īnstrūctum — equip, provide with everything needed

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.4.62: īnstruere et parāre convīvium omnibus rēbus (Lewis & Short)

    Of fitting out a house or a meal with everything needed.

Examples

  • tēgula pūblicē praebita est

    roof tiles were provided at public expenseLiv. 5.55.3

  • hae reī māteriem et quae opus sunt dominus praebēbit

    for this work the owner will provide the timber and whatever is neededCato Agr. 14

  • alicui virōs et arma ministrāre

    to supply someone with men and armsTraupman 388

See also provide for, require.
